t: LeetCode 2132 - Stamping the Grid: Prefix Sums Plus a Difference Array
o: **Understanding the problem.** Every empty (0) cell must lie under at least one stamp of fixed height h and width w, while no stamp may overlap an occupied (1) cell; stamps may overlap each other, cannot rotate, and must stay inside the grid. Example 1 succeeds because the empty region is a solid block that two overlapping 4x3 stamps blanket. Example 2 fails: the diagonal 1s chop the board into strips narrower than the 2x2 stamp, leaving some empty cells unreachable. Although m and n individually reach 10^5, the guarantee m*n <= 2*10^5 signals an O(mn)-style sweep with O(1) rectangle queries - i.e. 2-D prefix sums - rather than rescanning each candidate placement's full area.
k: A stamp fits anchored with bottom-right corner at (i,j) iff the h x w window ending there contains no 1 - an O(1) prefix-sum query.
Painting many rectangles then asking for per-cell coverage is exactly what a 2-D difference array is for.
Occupied cells must NOT be covered; only cells with grid value 0 need positive coverage.

a.i: Enumerate every legal top-left position, scan its h x w footprint for occupied cells, and if the window is clean mark all its empty cells as covered. Finally verify every empty cell got marked. This mirrors how a person would play the game and is correct, but each placement costs O(h*w), which explodes on large stamps.
s: For each top-left (r,c) with r+h <= m and c+w <= n, scan the h x w window for 1s.
If none found, set covered = true on every cell of that window.
After all placements, check each cell: it must be occupied or covered.
Return true only if no empty uncovered cell remains.
a.t: O(m*n*h*w) worst case - up to O(mn) placements each rescanning an h x w area

a.i: Two primitives collapse everything to three linear sweeps. First, build 2-D prefix sums P of the occupied flags so any window's sum - hence "does this stamp fit?" - is answered by four corner lookups. Second, instead of painting each valid stamp cell-by-cell, add four corner deltas (+1/-1 pattern) into a difference matrix D; a single in-place 2-D prefix sweep turns D into exact per-cell coverage counts. Every 0-cell must end with count >= 1.
s: Build prefix sums P over grid so rect_sum is inclusion-exclusion in O(1).
For each (i,j) with i >= h-1 and j >= w-1 whose h x w window sum is 0, add corner deltas to D for rows [i-h+1..i], cols [j-w+1..j].
Prefix-sum D in place so D[i][j] equals the number of stamps covering cell (i,j).
Return true iff every cell with grid[i][j] == 0 has D[i][j] > 0.
a.t: O(m*n) - prefix build, delta marking, and coverage sweep are each linear in the number of cells
a.sp: O(m*n) - the (m+1)x(n+1) prefix table and difference matrix

w: Narrate the two primitives - O(1) window occupancy via prefix sums, O(1) rectangle painting via a difference array - and the task collapses to linear sweeps; that decomposition is what interviewers want to hear. Pitfalls: mixing up top-left vs bottom-right anchoring (the stamped rectangle spans rows [i-h+1..i] and columns [j-w+1..j]), demanding coverage for OCCUPIED cells (they must stay untouched), and forgetting stamps cannot protrude outside the grid. Edge cases: stamps larger than the whole grid with any empty cell present means false; an all-occupied grid is trivially true. Follow-ups: minimize the stamp count, support multiple stamp sizes, or output one valid placement set from the difference array.
